hero.title: Friday
hero.lead: You land at 08:10. The rest is up to you :)

paras: Friday's free until Laurin and Olivia land at 9, so it's your call. Pick what looks good and I'll do the Planung (planning). Nothing that wrecks our legs before Sunday :)

arrival.title: You land
arrival.body: Leonardo Express to Termini, 32 min, €14, tap your card at the gate. I'll meet you for coffee around 09:45.

dinner.title: Dinner
dinner.body: Pizza at Li Rioni, behind the Colosseum.

options.title: Colosseum arena floor
options.line: You walk out onto the arena itself, where the fighters stood, with every tier looking down at you.

options.title: Nero's Golden House
options.line: Underground rooms of Nero's palace. A VR headset shows you the same rooms as they were, painted and full of light.

options.title: San Clemente
options.line: Two staircases down under a church: a Roman house, a temple of a secret cult, and water running somewhere below.

options.title: Pantheon
options.line: A 1,900-year-old dome with an open hole at the top. Stand in the middle and look up.

options.title: Castel Sant'Angelo
options.line: An emperor's tomb turned fortress. A long ramp and some stairs take you up to the terrace, St Peter's dead ahead.

options.title: Vittoriano roof
options.line: A glass lift to the top of the big white monument. All of Rome around you, the Forum right below.

options.title: Aventine keyhole
options.line: Look through a keyhole and St Peter's dome is framed in it. Next door, a terrace of orange trees over the river.

options.title: Pincio at sunset
options.line: We cut through Villa Borghese to a free terrace over Piazza del Popolo, watch the sun drop just right of St Peter's dome, then walk down Via Margutta.

options.title: Under the Trevi
options.line: Stairs down from an old cinema to a Roman house, where the water that feeds the Trevi still runs past.

options.title: Caesar's cats
options.line: The ruins where Caesar was stabbed are a cat sanctuary now. They sleep on the old stones.

options.title: Bone crypt
options.line: Six small rooms decorated with the bones of 3,700 friars, down to the chandeliers.

options.title: The nuns' bell
options.line: Ring a bell at a convent window and a nun hands you the key to a chapel painted in 1246, like a comic strip.

options.title: The trick corridor
options.line: A corridor that looks 35 metres long is about nine. Walk to the end and the statue is tiny.

options.title: The fake dome
options.line: The church never got its dome, so a painter faked one on the flat ceiling. From the marble disc it looks real.

options.title: The 17:30 machine
options.line: A 17th-century machine lowers a huge painting into the floor, with music, and a silver statue appears behind it.

options.title: Statues in a power plant
options.line: Roman marble gods stand between giant black engines in an old power station, and it's usually empty.

options.title: Pyramid and Keats
options.line: A quiet garden cemetery behind a real Roman pyramid. Keats is buried here.

options.title: Bernini at the Borghese
options.line: Marble that looks soft: Daphne's fingers turning into leaves, David biting his lip mid-throw.

options.title: Three Caravaggios
options.line: Walk in off a street near the Pantheon and three Caravaggios hang in a side chapel.

options.title: The Doria Pamphilj palace
options.line: A family still lives upstairs, and you walk through their gilded Hall of Mirrors to Velázquez's red-faced pope, with Bernini's bust of the same man beside it.

options.title: Keith Haring
options.line: A new show of his in a palace off Piazza Navona: the chalk subway drawings, a motorbike he painted in Rome, and a room under blacklight.

options.title: Trevi Fountain
options.line: The steps down to the basin are ticketed now, so it's calmer and you can get right up to the water.

options.title: Maritozzo
options.line: A soft bun split open and packed with cream, at Regoli near Termini, which has been making them since 1916.

options.title: Boccione
options.line: A tiny bakery in the Ghetto with no sign. Get the burnt-top fruit cake and the sour cherry tart.

options.title: Biscuit bakery
options.line: An old Trastevere bakery with a 15-metre oven. The trays come straight out to the counter.

options.title: Testaccio market
options.line: A neighbourhood market full of food stalls. The beef sandwich drips, so everyone eats standing up.

options.title: Supplì
options.line: Fried rice balls with mozzarella inside. Break one open and the cheese stretches like a phone cord.

options.title: Lunch at Fortunata
options.line: Women roll and cut pasta by hand in the front window. Ten minutes later it's on your plate.

options.title: Lunch in a hill of pots
options.line: A trattoria dug into a hill made of broken Roman jars. Ask for the inside room and they're behind glass by your table.

options.title: Pasta class
options.line: Roll and cut fettuccine by hand with a chef, then sit down and eat what you made. In English.

options.title: Aqueduct park
options.line: Roman aqueduct arches nearly 28 metres tall, standing in a field where locals run and walk their dogs.

options.title: Coppedè
options.line: A few streets most people never see. An iron chandelier hangs in a stone arch, and the fountain is all frogs.

options.title: Trastevere
options.line: Small ivy-covered streets across the river, two vintage shops on one street, and no plan: we turn wherever looks better.

options.title: The old centre
options.line: Piazza Navona to Campo de' Fiori through the small streets in between, past the Pantheon.

options.title: Monti
options.line: The neighbourhood above the Colosseum: a tiny chapel covered in gold mosaic, a fountain square, and vintage shops like Pifebo and Humana.

options.title: The Jewish Ghetto
options.line: A flat loop past a Roman colonnade with a church built into it, a palace sitting on a Roman theatre, and four bronze boys pushing turtles into a fountain. One thing: 16 October is the day in 1943 the Nazis rounded up the Ghetto, so expect wreaths and a quiet ceremony by the colonnade that day.

options.title: Appian Way by e-bike
options.line: E-bikes down a 2,300-year-old Roman road, past tombs and pine trees. Flat, and the bike does the work.

options.title: Chariot race in VR
options.line: On the real Circus Maximus track, a headset rebuilds the stands and a chariot race goes past you.

options.title: Noon cannon
options.line: A cannon fires below the Gianicolo terrace at noon. Loud, and the view of Rome is free.

options.title: Vespa sidecar
options.line: A driver takes you through the old streets in a vintage Vespa sidecar. You just sit and look.

options.title: Film Fest red carpet
options.line: The Rome Film Fest is on. Free seats in the open-air Cavea while the evening premiere walks the red carpet below.
options.tileSub: Free seats while the evening premiere arrives

options.title: A lap of the Circus Maximus
options.line: One easy shakeout lap of the old chariot track, about 1.5 km, with the Palatine ruins above you.
